newsitem.title: USA: US Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded steady late.
newsitem.headline: US Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded steady late.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded gasoline prices held their ground late Monday ahead of the seasonal changeover to summer-grade specifications, traders said.
With several refiners sighted in the market for prompt barrels, third-cycle winter-grade unleaded rallied against easing NYMEX front-month unleaded futures, traders said.
Chicago makes the seasonal switch to summer-grade unleaded on April 1.
Chicago winter-grade unleaded was bid 6.25 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded, with summer-grade barrels talked 2.75 cents a gallon higher in late-afternoon discussion.
Strength in the winter-grade barrels was attributed to refiner buying interest and diminishing inventories. "There's none to be had," one trader said earlier in the day.
Group Three unleaded gasoline eased to 3.25/3.0 cents a gallon under the print for late-month deliveries.
Low sulphur diesel was bid 4.0 cents a gallon over NYMEX April heating oil in Chicago and 4.25 cents over the print in Group Three.
